standard.title: Design a user interface
standard.description: Design a user interface for a digital system
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate, communicate and compare designs (AC9TDI4P03). They have produced design ideas and communicated them. They have not yet focused specifically on designing user interfaces — the layout, accessibility, and usability considerations of how a user interacts with a digital system.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students design a user interface for a digital system that addresses an identified need, considering layout, accessibility, and how users from different backgrounds can access the information.

nodes.label: What a user interface is and does
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that a user interface is the part of a digital system the user interacts with, and identify key elements of a user interface design
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three elements of a user interface (e.g. buttons, menus, input fields, labels) in an existing app or system; explain the purpose of each element
nodes.typical_width: Analyse an existing user interface (e.g. a school canteen ordering app) and identify how the layout, labels, and controls guide the user toward completing a task; discuss what would make it easier or harder to use
wider: Investigate how consistent symbols (copy, paste, save icons) across different apps help users from different cultural and language backgrounds — exploring what happens when symbols are ambiguous or culturally specific
Examine the user interface of a telehealth or community services platform designed for remote use — identifying which design decisions support access for users with limited digital literacy

response_modes.reason: Identifying UI elements across a range of apps (ordering, search, settings, navigation) builds the vocabulary students need to design with intent. Without having seen and named a range of element types, students default to what they know — typically a simple button grid — rather than selecting appropriate elements for the task.

success_criteria: Names at least three user interface elements correctly
Explains the purpose of each identified element
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify UI elements and their purposes cannot produce a purposeful design in N2 — interface design requires knowing what the components are and what they do for the user. Without N1, N2 produces decorative layouts rather than functional designs.

nodes.label: Designing a user interface for an identified need
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design a user interface (on paper or digitally) that addresses an identified user need
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a labelled sketch or digital mockup of a user interface for a specific purpose, showing the layout and key elements
nodes.typical_width: Design a user interface that addresses an identified need (from user stories); include layout, labels, navigation and key controls; explain how each design decision relates to what the user needs to do
wider: Design a user interface for the school canteen ordering app, then modify it for a user who is visually impaired — documenting changes to font size, colour contrast, and screen reader compatibility
Design a user interface intended for users from different cultural or language backgrounds — explaining how you used symbols, colour and layout to make it accessible across language differences

response_modes.reason: Students designing for themselves tend to produce interfaces that work for them but not for others. Designing for a specific, different user group (visually impaired, non-English speaking, remote community) makes the accessibility dimension concrete — it shifts design from personal preference to user-centred decision-making.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Designing for accessibility and cross-cultural usability is rich — it makes UI design decisions visibly principled rather than aesthetic, and the wider contexts (disability, language diversity, remote access) are each substantive design challenges in their own right.
success_criteria: Produces a labelled interface design showing key elements and layout
Explains how at least one design decision connects to the user's identified need
